card.name: Scholar names in ancient-history texts
card.fires_on: First or middle names and initials of scholars, translators or authors, right before their surname. The setting is a citation, bio or credit about ancient, classical or biblical topics.

modes.label: Author first names
modes.description: A first name in a byline, reference or bio about an ancient-world scholar or translator.
modes.example: About the Editor/Translator: <<Scott>> Goins, Ph.D., is Professor

modes.label: Initials and ampersands in citations
modes.description: A period after an initial or an ampersand joining co-authors in a reference to ancient texts.

modes.label: Dr. plus first name
modes.description: A first name after Dr. for a specialist in biblical or ancient studies.
modes.example: said Dr.<< Wayne>> Pitard, professor of the Hebrew Bible

card.writes: It pushes words like ancient and medieval, which fits the classical and historical subject of the surrounding text.
card.plain: It fires on a scholar's first name in a bibliography or bio when the topic is ancient history or classics.
